title: Reading estimates against zones
text: confidence interval already contains inferential information: range effects compatible data model. readers often lack reference frame magnitude. difference 0.5 kg large? odds ratio 1.4 worth acting ? Benchmarks answer question, imperfectly, putting behind interval shows interval benchmark together without merging verdict. verdict (“likely beneficial”, “trivial”) hides two things: interval lies relative threshold, arbitrary threshold . background shows . interval straddles boundary visibly ambiguous; soft, fading boundary visibly convention, natural discontinuity. basic plot, Tukey post-hoc comparison effect-size zones:  Two layers work, can use ggplot: geom_es_zones(): effect-size magnitude zones, symmetric around null. geom_mcid_zones(): harm / trivial / benefit zones minimal clinically important difference (MCID). Add zones layer first, points, error bars reference lines drawn top . default zones change axis limits: fill whatever range data define, outermost zones extend panel edges. Use expand = TRUE every cut-point visible.
code: fit <- aov(weight ~ group, data = PlantGrowth) plot_contrasts(   TukeyHSD(fit),   zones = geom_es_zones(es_benchmarks("cohen_d"), labels = TRUE),   model = fit ) #> ℹ Converting d thresholds with the model's pooled (residual) SD = 0.623. #>   Set `sd` in the zones layer to use a different SD.

text: 'ggplot2' extension draws interpretive background zones behind estimates confidence intervals forest plots, post-hoc contrast plots coefficient plots. Two modes provided: effect-size magnitude zones based published benchmark sets (e.g. Cohen, 1988, ISBN:0-8058-0283-5) clinical relevance zones based minimal clinically important difference (Jaeschke, Singer Guyatt, 1989 doi:10.1016/0197-2456(89)90005-6 ). package compute, classify reinterpret inference; draws background existing estimates intervals read.
